modified_files.summary: Appended exactly 17 exact-path rules for the G1-derived raw-byte consumers (124 -> 141): the G1 candidate checkpoint, manifest and change ledger; the five predeclared G1 governance role records; the G1 scope-authorization, execution-authorization and no-solve-evidence slots (evidence slot byte-preserving, the rest LF-pinned); the four role records the accepted R8 lifecycle record names; the 21l and FULLSTACK-01 suites. No rule removed or broadened, no wildcard, core.autocrlf unchanged.

Advanced the authorization lineage and candidate to G1; superseded the R8 candidate and the r3 authorization slot; added the G1 Main Full81 scope-authorization slot and a separate, fail-closed Full81 execution-authorization MECHANISM (resolver, validator, guard) that requires a frozen G1 lifecycle, a published G1 scope authorization and captured 21d no-solve evidence, published in that order. Mechanism only: no scope or execution authorization artifact exists or is created.

Re-pinned the seven pins whose targets carry G1 bytes (lifecycle overlay, authorization mechanism, .gitattributes, suites 21e/21f/21g/21h) and set their origin tag to the G1 candidate; added G1 re-pin notes; marked the R8 trust root and diagnostic historical-role table as R8-only provenance, kept byte-identical. 34 pins, 0 stale; no role names a future artifact.

Added the additive AuthorityGeneration G1 and advanced CURRENT_GENERATION to it (R8 retained byte-stable as historical); added the G1 closed-world candidate-manifest contract and change ledger, predeclared G1 governance role paths, the deterministic phase function, the three G1 identity axes with the intentional runtime-validation coupling declaration, and the matching raw-byte consumer universe extension. The validation-identity note on the 21i suite states that G1 creates it (phase-aware N-04 control) and that the raw SHA-256 recorded by the published R8 ledger remains historical evidence of the R8 run only.

Split the combined no-implicit-scope control into separate contracts: 21c has no implicit case scope (CASE_SCOPE_REQUIRED); the 21d no-solve preflight defaults to Full81 only behind the scope-authorization guard (live phase NOT_AUTHORIZED; scope-authorized disposable repository PASS with zero model constructions, optimizations and native-solver hits); 21d execution without an explicit case set is CASE_SCOPE_REQUIRED even when scope-authorized. The C0 real-repository execution-authorization premise is phase-aware from the source contract (current_generation_phase over G1_GOVERNANCE_STAGES): absent and refused before the lawful execution phase, a valid execution authorization over a frozen G1 lifecycle and a valid G1 scope authorization once reached, and failing closed on out-of-order presence. The A3 live-phase check is phase-aware too: once the G1 scope authorization is published, the guard grants the default only for a valid G1 scope authorization resolved against the frozen G1 lifecycle, and the same record resolved against no lifecycle grants nothing.

Made live-state assertions phase-aware: lifecycle, register, ownership and Full81 states are read from primary state (absent slot -> most restrictive state; present slot -> a valid accepted record is required). No assertion removed or relaxed.

Advanced current-generation assertions R8 -> G1, phase-aware; R8 asserted as the accepted, superseded historical predecessor; the durable-publication report check covers both the pre-package and the packaged phase.

Retargeted the substitution attacks to G1: structural attacks against the predeclared G1 role paths in the real repository, authenticity attacks in a disposable G1 repository. Every attack case retained. The no-premature-governance-artifact check is phase-aware from the source contract (current_generation_phase over G1_GOVERNANCE_STAGES): the lawful audit and acceptance intermediate phases pass, out-of-order presence fails closed, and a present lifecycle record must be a valid acceptance; a disposable-fixture phase matrix proves four lawful phases pass and eight out-of-order states fail closed. The live deployment-gate check is phase-aware: before a lawful G1 execution authorization the gate refuses Full81 (scope guard, then execution guard); once one is published it admits Full81 only for a valid G1 lifecycle, scope and execution chain, with no native solver entry; A2 stays hard-blocked in every phase.

The promotion fixture synthesizes a G1 candidate package with role records at the predeclared G1 paths; contract V4 retained as a historical control on R8; real-repository unauthorized checks made phase-aware. No negative control deleted or relaxed. The positive-control execution-interlock checks decide on the fixture repository, which holds no execution authorization in any phase; the real deployment-gate check refuses Full81 before a lawful G1 execution authorization and, once one is published, admits Full81 only for a valid G1 chain, with no native solver entry.

Created in G1: absent from the predecessor commit. The R8-era bytes, whose raw SHA-256 the published R8 candidate change ledger recorded, are not published by G1, and that R8 record remains historical evidence of the R8 run only. The N-04 control T5 is phase-aware from the source contract: a disposable repository with a frozen G1 lifecycle and no scope authorization proves N-04 in every phase; the real entrypoint fails closed until the G1 scope authorization is published, then passes only for a valid authorization and never reaches the execution callee.

New G1 suite: generation contract, candidate phase, G1 content contract and change ledger, validation-generation separation, lifecycle promotion, scope-slot isolation, execution guard, raw-byte/EOL coverage, identity axes, acyclic binding and no-solve surface. Its real-repository premises (promotion isolation, the candidate-only lifecycle control and the no-future-identity check) are phase-aware from the source contract (current_generation_phase over G1_GOVERNANCE_STAGES): absent before their lawful phase, valid by the live resolvers once reached, and failing closed on out-of-order presence. Its change-set reproduction derives the 21i class from published evidence (CREATE: the bytes differ from the R8-recorded raw SHA-256), and the publication-source attacks run on a synthetic PUBLISH_UNCHANGED entry that the production validator first accepts.

fullstack_01_reference.relationship: Accepted predecessor authority for the four canonical Full81 execution inputs. G1 carries those four input pins unchanged in G1_GOVERNANCE_AUTHORITY_IDENTITY and in the runtime authorization mechanism; it binds no FULLSTACK-01 frozen digest as a live G1 identity.

predecessor.known_historical_inconsistency: Two historical observations, carried for the independent auditor and NOT resolved by this candidate. (1) Predecessor freeze coverage: the accepted R8 lifecycle (published 0291171424d2654cfe9ac3c8ffaa773e163c75be) froze an implementation identity whose 21c and 21d entries name runner bytes first published at 222685f0ea8a1a9f281e30962e223a339d5ec938, not the bytes of the R8 publication commits; the accepted FULLSTACK-01 lifecycle (published 8acb5ce9217c36eca0fc89989be8329c5453f3cc) froze exactly the runtime bytes of 82f04841ef0861c079eca57d9688e6cad3caadc6; commit 222685f then changed 21c and 21d after that re-freeze. At the G1 predecessor commit the published runtime bytes therefore equal neither predecessor's frozen implementation identity. G1 binds neither frozen identity as a live binding: its runtime identity is computed from live bytes and R8 material appears only as typed historical evidence. (2) Stack origin label: src/production_successor_stack_v7_3.py is pinned in the authority bundle with the historical origin tag U_06_ALIGNMENT_CANDIDATE_R3, although Git shows the stack's bytes last changed at 02b998b (Main Full81 authorization mechanism R2), after U-06 R3. The tag is carried-forward predecessor metadata, unchanged and unread by any guard; G1 neither modifies the stack nor re-tags the pin. Left for the auditor to judge.
